title: Cerebellar optogenetic stimulation restores motor cortex activity and behaviour after stroke
title_zh: 小脑光遗传刺激在中风后恢复运动皮层活动和行为
abstract: Abstract Stroke causes severe motor deficits, but functional recovery can occur through neural circuit reorganization in areas adjacent to and remote from the infarct. Optogenetic stimulation can modulate neuronal activity and improve recovery in experimental models, yet the population-level cortical dynamics underlying these effects remain poorly understood. The lateral cerebellar nucleus projects to the cortex via the dentatothalamocortical pathway and represents a promising target for remote neuromodulation after stroke. We performed longitudinal one-photon calcium imaging of ipsilesional primary motor cortex layer V neurons in awake, behaving mice (n = 13) following transient middle cerebral artery occlusion. Mice received optogenetic stimulation of the contralesional lateral cerebellar nucleus using CaMKII-driven Channelrhodopsin-2 on post-stroke days 5 through 14. Stimulation-treated and non-stimulated stroke mice were compared across behavioral and neural activity measures for up to 28 days post-stroke. Stroke significantly reduced ipsilesional motor cortex population activity during the subacute phase, with decreased calcium peak frequency (p < 0.001) and amplitude (p = 0.004). Reduced frequency was strongly associated with lesion size at post-stroke day 6 (r² = 0.88, p < 0.001), and reduced amplitude was similarly associated with lesion size at post-stroke day 9 (r² = 0.39, p = 0.022). Cerebellar stimulation counteracted these deficits, significantly increasing both frequency (p = 0.017) and amplitude (p < 0.001) and improving behavioral recovery on the rotating beam task (p = 0.027). Critically, in stimulated animals, motor cortex activity was no longer coupled to lesion size, indicating that stimulation decoupled cortical dynamics from injury severity. Early post-stroke functional connection density among motor cortex neurons predicted long-term behavioral outcome in non-stimulated animals (r² = 0.50, p = 0.033), but this relationship was abolished by stimulation, suggesting that cerebellar stimulation reshaped the recovery trajectory independently of initial network disruption. Stroke also shifted neuronal populations toward minimally active states, and stimulation preserved a higher proportion of moderately active neurons (p = 0.029). These findings define population-level changes in peri-lesional motor cortex after stroke at cellular resolution and demonstrate that cerebellar optogenetic stimulation counteracts stroke-induced cortical dysfunction, decouples recovery from lesion burden, and promotes functional recovery.
abstract_zh: 摘要 中风会导致严重的运动缺陷，但功能恢复可通过梗死周围及远端区域的神经环路重组实现。光遗传刺激可以调节神经元活动并在实验模型中改善恢复，但其背后的人群水平皮层动力学尚不清楚。小脑侧核经齿状丘脑皮质通路投射到皮层，是中风后远程神经调节的有望靶点。我们在短暂性中大脑动脉栓塞后，对清醒活动小鼠（n = 13）侧病侧初级运动皮层第V层神经元进行了纵向单光子钙成像。小鼠在中风后第5至14天接受使用CaMKII驱动的Channelrhodopsin-2对悖病侧小脑侧核进行光遗传刺激。接受刺激与未受刺激的中风小鼠在中风后长达28天的行为和神经活动指标上进行比较。中风显著降低了亚急性期侧病侧运动皮层群体活动，钙峰频率降低（p < 0.001），幅度降低（p = 0.004）。频率降低与中风后第6天梗死体积强相关（r² = 0.88，p < 0.001），幅度降低同样与中风后第9天梗死体积相关（r² = 0.39，p = 0.022）。小脑刺激抵消了这些缺陷，显著增加频率（p = 0.017）和幅度（p < 0.001），并改善旋转梁任务的行为恢复（p = 0.027）。关键的是，在受刺激动物中，运动皮层活动不再与梗死体积耦合，表明刺激使皮层动力学与损伤严重程度解耦。中风后早期运动皮层神经元之间的功能连接密度预测了未受刺激动物的长期行为结局（r² = 0.50，p = 0.033），但该关系被刺激消除，提示小脑刺激独立于初始网络破坏而重塑恢复轨迹。中风还使神经元群体转向低活跃状态，刺激保留了更高比例的中度活跃神经元（p = 0.029）。这些发现以细胞分辨率界定了中风后病灶周围运动皮层的人群水平变化，并证明小脑光遗传刺激可抵消中风引起的皮层功能障碍，使恢复与梗死负担解耦，并促进功能恢复。
